metadata.title: Continuation Ratio Model for Polytomous Responses with Censored Like Latent Classes
metadata.venue: Quantitative Psychology (Springer Proceedings in Mathematics & Statistics 422)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The analysis uses ICCS 2016 data with a two-stage sampling design (schools sampled, then students within selected schools). To account for the complex sampling design, the authors scaled survey weights so that each country contributes equally to model estimation. In the Mplus syntax, the weight variable is explicitly used (WEIGHT = ws) and the clustering structure is handled via CLUSTER = id_j with STRATIFICATION = id_s. The model is estimated with MLR and uses Taylor Series Linearization to obtain standard errors that reflect the sampling design; therefore, population-representative inference is supported under the ICCS design assumptions.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This chapter models polytomous bullying victimization responses using a mixture continuation ratio response model (M-CRM) and does not use PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. Plausible Values are therefore not applicable because the dependent variables are item-level bullying frequency categories (expanded into continuation-ratio pseudo-items), not ILSA cognitive achievement scales with PVs. Missing-data handling is not reported in the provided text because the focus is on the proposed response model and its fitting under ICCS complex sampling; the excerpt does not specify an imputation or deletion rule for missing responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The empirical illustration uses ICCS 2016 bullying victimization items (“Students’ experience of physical and verbal abuse at school”, bul1–bul6) and restricts the analysis to the Latin American participating samples: Chile, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Mexico, and Peru. Responses are modeled as polytomous categories (not at all, once, 2–4 times, 5 times or more) and then expanded into k-1 continuation-ratio pseudo-items in wide format (bul1_0–bul6_2). The model is fitted to the pooled multi-country sample with survey weights scaled so each country contributes equally, and standard errors are computed using Taylor Series Linearization under the ICCS two-stage sampling design (stratification and clustering).

data.outcome_summary: This chapter proposes a mixture continuation ratio response model (M-CRM) to handle polytomous bullying victimization responses with a censored-like latent distribution, motivated by the high accumulation of “not at all” responses across bullying items in ICCS 2016. The empirical application uses ICCS 2016 bullying items (bul1–bul6) from five Latin American countries (Chile, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Mexico, Peru) and expands each polytomous item into continuation-ratio pseudo-items for modeling. The authors fit the model in Mplus using pseudo maximum likelihood with complex sampling adjustments (WEIGHT=ws, CLUSTER=id_j, STRATIFICATION=id_s) and select the number of latent classes using the Vuong–Lo–Mendell–Rubin likelihood ratio test (favoring three classes). The results are used to describe item-side bullying event frequencies, person-side bullying risk profiles via mixture classes, and class differences in expected response proportions, while also enabling estimation of population prevalence of bullying events. The chapter emphasizes modeling advantages over sum-score approaches, but it does not report predictive ML metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) in the provided excerpt.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a methodological modeling chapter using ICCS 2016 item-response data rather than an ML predictive study with a supervised target and reported predictive performance metrics. Consequently, fields such as ml_techniques and main_findings (structured predictive findings) are intentionally left empty because the excerpt does not describe a predictive ML pipeline, target variable, or evaluation metrics like accuracy or AUC. The focus is on statistical model specification, estimation under complex survey design, and substantive interpretation of latent bullying risk profiles and prevalence.
